common_name: Alcazar Red Hot Poker (Vivid Orange-Red Kniphofia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage is critical, especially in winter, since red hot poker rots in waterlogged conditions.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage is critical year-round but especially in winter, when standing moisture around the crown quickly causes rot. Alcazar bears dense, torch-like flower spikes in a vivid, saturated orange-red that holds its intense color from bud through the full bloom period, rather than shifting through the red-to-yellow gradient typical of many red hot poker cultivars, held on sturdy stems above grassy, arching foliage from summer into fall. The tubular flowers are a favorite of hummingbirds, which visit reliably through the bloom season. In colder parts of its range, tie the leaves together over the crown and mulch deeply before the first hard freeze to protect the growing point, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring if flowering declines.

common_name: Flamenco Red Hot Poker (Mixed Yellow-Orange-Red Seed Strain)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost and transplant after all frost danger has passed; Flamenco is a mixed-color seed strain producing a range of yellow, orange, and red-flowered plants.

directions: Sow seed 1/8 inch deep and keep evenly moist at 65-75°F until germination, then plant in well-drained soil in full sun once frost danger has passed. Flamenco is a mixed seed strain producing a colorful range of torch-like flower spikes across a planting, from clear yellow through orange to red, with many individual spikes showing the classic two-toned gradient as florets open from the base upward, all held on sturdy stems above grassy, arching foliage. The tubular flowers draw hummingbirds reliably through the summer and fall bloom season. Because it is grown from seed, individual plants vary in exact color, giving informal drifts extra visual variety. In colder parts of its range, tie foliage together and mulch deeply over the crown before the first hard freeze to protect the growing point.

common_name: Mango Popsicle Red Hot Poker (Compact Orange Dwarf Kniphofia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Mango Popsicle is a compact, dwarf red hot poker bred for smaller borders and container growing.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage is essential year-round, since standing moisture around the crown quickly causes rot. Mango Popsicle bears compact, torch-like flower spikes in warm mango-orange, blooming on a much shorter, more compact plant than traditional tall red hot poker cultivars, which suits it well to smaller borders, rock gardens, and large containers where a full-size Kniphofia would be out of scale. Its shorter grassy foliage and reduced overall size also make winter protection easier in colder parts of its range. The tubular flowers attract hummingbirds through the summer bloom season. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring if flowering begins to decline.

common_name: Fire Dance Red Hot Poker (Dwarf Red-Orange Kniphofia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Fire Dance is a dwarf red hot poker with an extended bloom season compared to older, single-flush cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage is critical year-round, since red hot poker rots in waterlogged soil. Fire Dance produces compact torch-like spikes opening bright red in bud and aging to orange, creating the classic two-toned effect on a dwarf, sturdy plant that blooms repeatedly over an extended season from early summer well into fall, longer than many older red hot poker cultivars that flower in a single flush. Its compact size fits smaller borders and mass plantings, and the tubular flowers draw hummingbirds reliably throughout the long bloom period. In colder parts of its range, tie the grassy foliage together over the crown and mulch deeply before the first hard freeze, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring if flowering declines.

common_name: Percy's Pride Red Hot Poker (Unusual Pale Yellow-Green Kniphofia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Percy's Pride bears unusual pale yellow-green flowers, a departure from the typical hot reds and oranges of the genus.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage is critical year-round, since standing moisture around the crown quickly causes rot. Percy's Pride bears tall, torch-like flower spikes in an unusual pale, cool yellow-green shade, a striking departure from the hot reds, oranges, and golds typical of red hot poker cultivars, giving it a softer, more sophisticated presence in the border. Its long, arching, grassy foliage and tall flower stems make a strong architectural statement from summer into fall, and the tubular flowers draw hummingbirds despite the unusually cool color. In colder parts of its range, tie the foliage together over the crown and mulch deeply before the first hard freeze to protect the growing point, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring if flowering declines.
